title: Generating Chemically Competent E. coli Cells
author: Su Yin Phua
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.666hhhe
materials: Filter sterilize (stericup) both solutions and store @ 4ºC. MOPS degrades into unknown yellow byproduct from autoclaving!

steps.title: Prepare Solution A (250 mL)
steps.instruction: In a beaker dissolve 5.08 g MgCl₂·6H₂O (or 2.38 g anhydrous MgCl₂) and 0.52 g MOPS in ~250 mL deionized water, adjust pH to 7.0 with ~900 µL 1 M NaOH, then transfer to a measuring cylinder and bring the final volume to exactly 250 mL.

steps.title: Prepare Solution B (300 mL)
steps.instruction: In a separate beaker dissolve 0.61 g MgCl₂·6H₂O (or 0.29 g anhydrous MgCl₂), 6.78 g MOPS, and 2.21 g CaCl₂·2H₂O in ~300 mL deionized water, adjust pH to 6.5 with ~6.8 mL 1 M NaOH, then transfer to a measuring cylinder and bring the final volume to exactly 300 mL.

steps.title: Inoculate LB and add MgSO₄
steps.instruction: Add an aliquot (or the entire 5 mL) of the overnight starter culture to the desired volume of fresh LB (anywhere from 50 mL to 500 mL) in a suitable flask (e.g., 250 mL conical for 50 mL, 1–2 L conical for 500 mL) to ensure good aeration, then add autoclaved MgSO₄ to achieve a final concentration of 10 mM.

steps.title: Grow culture to OD₆₀₀ 0.4‑0.5
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated LB at 37 °C with shaking until the optical density at 600 nm reaches 0.4–0.5 (do not exceed 0.6); this typically takes 1–4 hours depending on the culture volume (e.g., ~1 hour for a 5 mL starter to reach OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.5).

steps.title: Ice‑chill culture
steps.instruction: Place the culture on ice for 10 minutes, ensuring that a refrigerated centrifuge is ready for the next step.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the chilled culture at 4 °C for 10 minutes at approximately 4,200 × g (rcf).

steps.title: Resuspend in cold Solution A
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the cell pellet in cold Solution A; use 250 mL of Solution A for a 500 mL culture or 25 mL for a 50 mL culture (adjust proportionally).

steps.title: Incubate cells on ice
steps.instruction: Divide the resuspended cells equally among pre‑chilled centrifuge bottles or Falcon tubes and incubate at 4 °C for 10–20 minutes.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again at 4 °C for 10 minutes at ~4,200 × g.

steps.title: Resuspend in Solution B + glycerol
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 4.3 mL of cold Solution B together with 700 µL glycerol, adding the glycerol slowly with a pipette.

steps.title: Optional second wash in Solution B
steps.instruction: If desired, remove the supernatant and resuspend the cells again in cold Solution B (repeat the same volume as used for the initial Solution A resuspension).

steps.title: Incubate 30 min at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Allow the cells to sit on ice for 30 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Third centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cells a final time at 4 °C for 10 minutes at ~4,200 × g.

steps.title: Aliquot and freeze competent cells
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, then aliquot the cell suspension into pre‑chilled tubes (20 µL, 50 µL, or 200 µL as needed). Immediately plunge the aliquots into liquid nitrogen, then store them at –80 °C for long‑term use.
